questions.q: What is the key difference between Lesson 15's CLI commands and Infrastructure as Code?
options: CLI commands are imperative (typed steps); IaC describes the end state you want and lets a tool figure out what to do
There is no real difference — they are exactly the same approach
IaC can only be used with the Azure Portal, never the CLI
CLI commands describe an end state; IaC types individual steps
questions.explain: IaC's key benefit is that running the same description twice doesn't break anything the second time.

options: Azure's native Infrastructure as Code format, written in JSON
A graphical drag-and-drop tool inside the Azure Portal
A type of virtual machine size
A billing report generated by Cost Management
questions.explain: Everything done through the Portal or CLI ultimately goes through the same Azure Resource Manager engine ARM templates talk to directly.

questions.q: What is the actual relationship between Bicep and an ARM template?
options: Bicep is a friendlier language that compiles down to the exact same ARM JSON underneath
Bicep and ARM templates are two completely unrelated, incompatible systems
ARM templates compile down into Bicep at deployment time
Bicep replaces ARM entirely and Azure no longer supports ARM templates
questions.explain: Nothing is lost or different at deployment time — Bicep is purely a nicer way to author the same result.

questions.q: Why does this lesson stay conceptual instead of having you author a real Bicep file?
options: The Terraform & Bicep for Data Engineers course in this catalog covers Bicep authoring in real depth already
Bicep cannot actually be used to deploy real Azure resources
This course does not expect students to ever use Infrastructure as Code
ARM templates have been fully deprecated by Microsoft
questions.explain: This is a conceptual overview meant to build vocabulary before a dedicated course covers hands-on authoring.

questions.q: Why is raw ARM JSON often considered harder to work with than Bicep?
options: ARM JSON is verbose — even simple resources take dozens of lines of nested brackets and quotes
ARM JSON cannot describe resource relationships at all
ARM JSON is not supported by Azure Resource Manager
Bicep and ARM JSON produce different deployed resources
questions.explain: Bicep is shorter, easier to read, and catches more mistakes before deployment, while compiling to identical ARM JSON.
